title: Petri pocket run digest — personal experiment ledger
content:
Quick personal ledger for small-loop inference probes (petri-style micro runs). Purpose: capture tiny sweep results, heuristics, and unpolished notes so I can later lift signals into the main eval harness. Not for public consumption — rough numbers, shorthand, TODOs.

Run summary table (most recent at top):
| date | run-id | model | q | batch | req-toks | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | cost-est ($/k tokens) | notes |
|------|--------|-------|---:|------:|--------:|-------:|--------:|----------------------:|-------|
| 2025-03-02 | petri-032 | redwood-1.4b | 8bit | 4 | 128 | 48 | 120 | 0.006 | prefix cache hit ~60% on repeat prompts; token growth -> p95 spike
| 2025-02-28 | petri-028 | rwx-7b | fp16 | 1 | 256 | 110 | 245 | 0.022 | single-shot, kv warmup overhead evident; try pre-warm step
| 2025-02-25 | petri-021 | rwx-7b | 4bit | 8 | 64 | 35 | 90 | 0.0045 | batched nicely, quality diffs small vs fp16 for short prompts

Quick hypotheses/observations:
- 8bit quant gives the best cost/latency balance for short conversational bursts, but p95 sensitive to cold KV cache.
- Batching >4 benefits throughput but increases p50 for single-request latency-sensitive paths.
- Pre-warm (single dummy request per worker) reduces p95 on rwx-7b by ~15-20% in quick checks.

Short checklist (actionable):
- [ ] Add a scripted pre-warm step to microbench harness (small request -> drop) (ticket ENG-1173)
- [x] Push petri-028 logs to /repro/petri/ (manually copied 2025-03-01)
- [ ] Run 100-repeat prefix-cache stability sweep for 8bit vs fp16 (focus p95)
- [ ] Calibrate cost-est calc to include KV memory reclamation overhead

Scratch math (very rough):
- cost-est = baseline-token-rate * model-cost-factor / 1000
- baseline-token-rate observed ~0.0012 $/token for rwx-7b fp16 at low batch => aligns to 0.022 $/k tokens in the table above.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Why does kv-cache hit % vary so much with prompt framing? (maybe tokenizer boundary behavior) -> try identical seed prompt across variants and enforce whitespace normalization.
- Should we expose a warmup hint in SDK (small best-effort call) for latency SLO customers? Track adoption telemetry if added.

Links and quick references:
- local repro dir: ~/repro/petri/ (contains raw logs, traces, perf-summary.csv)
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro/pull/452 (adds bench harness glue)
- ticket for rollout: ENG-1173

Last quick observations (2025-03-03):
- Did a 50-run loop with 8bit + batch=4 => median stable, but two outliers at ~400ms p95 correlated with worker GC spikes (need to capture full trace and host metrics).

If I can't get time to formalize: push top 3 rows into shared eval spreadsheet and tag @applied-ml for follow-up next week.

End of ledger entry.
